messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

We will be meeting this Thursday (6/5) from 10-noon virtually and in person in the DataLab classroom (Library 360). This is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time. Additionally, if there are topics you would like to see someone do a deeper dive on, let us know!

Datalab will also be open for Tea Time on Thursday afternoon as well.

D-RUG: 10am-noon, DataLab Classroom, Library 360, and zoom https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09
Tea Time: 1-2pm, DataLab Classroom, Library 360

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.subject: Call for Ecological Researchers who want to deepen their R skills
messages.subject_clean: Call for Ecological Researchers who want to deepen their R skills
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGies!

There is a great opportunity <https://deltacouncil.ca.gov/delta-science-program/science-synthesis-working-group> coming up to level up your R coding skills.

The Delta Science Program is partnering with the National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis (NCEAS) for the third time to lead a collaborative synthesis working group. The synthesis working group delivers high-quality training in synthetic data science, and statistical techniques and provides a focused opportunity for enhanced collaboration between scientists from federal and State agencies as well as academic scientists. The trainings are free but there is no funding provided for participation or travel.

The 2023 training <https://learning.nceas.ucsb.edu/2023-10-delta/> included topics like mapping census data, parallel processing, git workflows, making web apps and dashboards with shiny, reproducible and automated workflows with targets, and publishing data.

The Delta Science Program is also looking for synthesis topic ideas for an upcoming synthesis working group in the fall of 2025. Please note that this is not an opportunity to collect data. Submissions should focus on identifying questions for which existing, publicly available data can be leveraged to inform Bay-Delta management needs. Ideas can be submitted by anyone, even those unable to participate in the working group.

Previous working group participants convened for three weeks of training and collaboration facilitated by experts from NCEAS. Following this working group event, participants analyzed and synthesized data using their newly developed skills to address questions important to Bay-Delta management. Outputs from the effort include multiple publications, reproducible workflows, R functions, and derived data.
Full announcement <https://deltacouncil.ca.gov/pdf/science-program/2025-delta-synthesis-working-group-announcement.pdf>
Call for Participants <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdItT642YhFAGeFpQCKSfhycYDG09Sy4vDH7xjXOpScZXDu3g/viewform>
Call for Synthesis Projects <https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf6FDeRzhOepSn3XlWLTYvtU2uRQAzz0YGr9epAbMqsC6WNyg/viewform>
Cheers,
Elise

messages.subject: Goodbyes, Hellos, and Summer D-RUG
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies,

Tara Pozzi, long time member and CooRdinator, has finished her Ph.D. on effective environmental governance and will be moving on to greener pastures. However, she is not leaving us quite yet, so please congratulate her if you see her at D-RUG over the next few weeks.

Additionally, Jenny Cribbs of the Ecology Grad Group and active D-RUG member, is our newest cooRdinator! Yay!

We are now in summer schedule D-RUG. That means we will be primarily remote (fully remote this Thursday 6/26). However, people have expressed interest in meeting up in person, both in Davis and Sacramento. If you would like to have input on these in person meetups (when and where they happen), please join us on the r-users-group <https://join.slack.com/share/enQtOTExMDY4MTYxNzI5Ny0xYjM0N2ZmODA4ZmM0NDE5ZTE2NTVkMGUxZmYwYTZmYWZhZjZlZDNiZWJiMDNmNjNlODhmZjkxZmZjNDFhYjhk> slack channel on the UC Davis slack.

Zoom Link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

Welcome to summer!
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators
